title: A machine for the canonical guard check
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine $C$, three pairwise distinct states called entry, yes, and no, and a natural number $a$, with at least four work tapes, such that for any Boolean strings $\alpha$, $bits$, and $rest$ for which $\alpha$ parses as $bits$ and $rest$, the machine started on $\alpha$ with its entry state and blank work tapes reaches, at some time $t\le a(|\alpha|+1)$, the yes state if $\max\{guard,(4k+5)3^{k+1}\}(v+1)\le |rest|$ and the no state otherwise, where $k$ is the work-tape count of $F$ and $v$ is the binary value of $bits$. It has produced no output; its input-head position is $2|bits|+3$ in the yes case and $|\alpha|+1$ in the no case. Every work tape except tape $1$ is at position zero and contains the canonical count word for $bits$ on tape $0$, the canonical offset word for $bits$ on tape $2$, and the empty word on all remaining tapes.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Boolean-alphabet machine, distinct entry/yes/no states, and a natural number $a$
The machine has at least four work tapes
The three states are pairwise distinct
There exists a time bounded by $a(|\alpha|+1)$ with the specified state, output, input-head position, and work-tape conditions
